direct_answer: There is no single secret to living long with arthritis. Regular activity, strength exercise, eating well, sleep, social contact, not smoking and regular medicine reviews support health and independence.

content:
Small habits add up over time.

This guide covers evidence-based basics. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Move regularly

Follow activity guidance for older adults, including strength and balance.

Eat well

A balanced diet and enough protein help muscles.

Sleep

Ask for help with night pain affecting sleep.

Stay connected

Social contact supports wellbeing.

Review medicines

Ask for a review yearly or when things change.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can habits slow arthritis?

They help symptoms and function.

Is it too late to start?

No.

Sources and further reading

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
